messages:
Sam Briggs: FYI - getting an escalation from AcmeCorp. They say p95/p99 for our text-gen endpoint jumped after yesterday's quant profile rollout (qprofile_int8_v2). Previously p95 ~80ms, now p95 ~420ms, p99 ~1.2s on some requests. Happening on their Dedicated pool (A100s) in us-west-2. 

Carlos Romero: Ack. Customer provided a small repro and traced it to requests that hit >512 token context. Short prompts still OK, long-context requests show worst tail.

model-ops-bot: Deploy event: qprofile_int8_v2 applied to pool dedicated-us-west-2 at 2026-02-27T18:24:12Z by deploy/quant-automations.

Priya Nair: Thanks Sam. Initial hunch: int8 path may trigger a slower fallback kernel for certain layer shapes (esp large context) or calibration mismatch causing per-token recompute. Also need to check whether fp8 toggle landed accidentally for some shards.

Ethan Liu: I pulled runtime traces from a repro request Sam attached. Key lines: 
```
kernel_select: quantized_int8_conv -> success
kv_cache_hit: false
kernel_fallback: true (reason: unsupported tile size)
scheduling_path: scalar_emulation
per_token_time_ms: 8.3 (avg) -> 35.6 (tail)
```
That kernel_fallback line is the smoking gun — it means we tried int8 optimized kernel, then fell back to generic emulation which is much slower.

Sam Briggs: Repro (customer): 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-text-3b","quant_profile":"qprofile_int8_v2","input":"<long-context>...","max_tokens":128}'
```
They said forcing no quant via query param brought latency back: quant=false or setting quant_profile=fp16_fixed restored p95 to ~90ms.

Priya Nair: Two immediate asks: (1) Can we confirm which hardware/kernel combos cause fallback? (2) Suggest a safe mitigation: rollback qprofile_int8_v2 for that pool OR enable fallback_to_fp16 for the profile so we don't hit slow emulation path.

Ethan Liu: I checked kernel matrix. int8 optimized kernels currently target H100 tensor cores and certain A100 firmware/kernel versions. On older A100 drivers a path can be unsupported -> fallback to scalar_emulation. The profile was rolled out cluster-wide without restricting to hardware. That was a mistake.

Priya Nair: Ok. Quick mitigation plan: 
- Immediately toggle profile routing to exclude dedicated-us-west-2 (or mark pool incompatible) -> rollback on control plane. 
- Add a per-profile flag "enforce_native_kernel=true" and, if not available, route to fp16.
- For customer: enable per-API override to force fp16 (runtime_override.force_dtype=\"fp16\") until we fix.

Sam Briggs: Customer wants timeline. Can we estimate how long to rollback and how long to test a corrected profile?

Ethan Liu: Rollback is trivial: mark qprofile_int8_v2 inactive for that pool in control plane -> seconds. Testing corrected profile (restricting to H100/driver-min) + calibration re-run: ~4-6 hours. Full canary with perf metrics: 24 hours.

Carlos Romero: I'll tell AcmeCorp: we can toggle a mitigation now (force fp16 override per-customer) and follow up with a more durable fix. Any suggested language?

Priya Nair: Suggested message: "We observed that the quantization profile was applied to hardware combinations that do not support the optimized int8 kernels, causing kernel fallback and tail latency spikes. We've rolled back that profile on your pool and can enable an fp16 override for your account immediately while we validate a hardware-restricted profile. We expect testing to complete within 6 hours and full re-deploy in 24 hours."

model-ops-bot: Alert: calibration job for qprofile_int8_v2 failed on shard 7/32 (overflow during histogram collection) at 2026-02-27T18:20:01Z.

Ethan Liu: Also saw calibration anomalies in the CI logs — some layers produced NaNs during activation quant histogram step (likely dynamic range mismatch). Forcing a per-layer clip or re-running calibration on a smaller representative dataset should help.

Sam Briggs: Repro steps we sent to customer (doable on their side): 
1) Run the curl repro with quant_profile=qprofile_int8_v2 and capture X-Redwood-Latency header.
2) Run again with runtime_override.force_dtype=\"fp16\" or quant_profile=\"fp16_safe_v1\" and compare.
3) Send us a flamegraph from "/debug/trace?reqid=..." if possible.

Carlos Romero: Customer tried fp16 override and p95 dropped back to ~95ms. They gave logs showing kernel_fallback entries. They're happy for a temporary fp16 override.

Priya Nair: Long-term fixes: 
- Update profile rollout flow: require hardware capability gating (kernel matrix) before applying quant profiles. 
- Add a runtime guard: if quant kernel fallback would be triggered for a request path, automatically use fp16/force_native=true route instead of scalar emulation. 
- Improve calibration: add pre-deploy synthetic calibration step that detects NaNs/overflows and rejects the profile.

Ethan Liu: Also consider providing a lighter-weight int8 profile (qprofile_int8_safe) that uses per-layer mixed precision where problematic layers remain fp16. That often preserves latency/quality tradeoffs without triggering fallback.

Sam Briggs: For the immediate customer-facing action I've done the per-account override and sent the suggested message. They'll monitor.

Priya Nair: I'll file an infra ticket to roll back the profile from that pool and add the gating. Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-ml to own kernel compatibility matrix + calibration hardening. ETA on rollback: 10m.

Ethan Liu: I'll re-run calibration with extended clipping and per-layer keep-fp16 for the failing layers, test on A100 matrix, and produce a qprofile_int8_safe build.

Carlos Romero: Thanks all. Customer is appreciative of the quick mitigation. Will keep this thread updated if they see regressions after fix. :thumbsup:
